text.prompt: When should your fretting hand squeeze?
text.why: Squeeze to land, relax to move. Constant force wears out your hand in minutes.

text.prompt: What makes a scratch?
options: Fretting fingers resting lightly on the strings
text.why: Touching without pressing stops the strings from ringing. The strum turns into a crisp, percussive click.

text.why: A short tip gives you control and a clean sound. Too much pick snags on the paired strings.

text.prompt: Which pair is the highest in pitch?
text.why: Pairs count from the highest, pair 1, to the lowest, pair 4.

text.prompt: What comes after G in the D major scale?
text.why: After G on pair 3 comes A. Play it on the open A pair rather than reaching for fret 7.

text.prompt: What makes a good tremolo?
text.why: Keep the pick close to the strings and the strokes even. Speed comes later, once the motion is relaxed.

text.prompt: Why does it matter that no pair rings open?
options: You can silence it by easing off
It keeps the chord in tune
text.why: With every pair held down, relaxing your fingers stops the sound at once. That is the secret of the chop.

text.prompt: Your chop keeps ringing. What fixes it?
options: Lift your fingers off the neck
Ease off with your fretting fingers sooner
text.why: The chop is choked by the fretting hand. Relax the pressure but keep your fingertips on the strings.

text.prompt: Where does the high part begin?
options: On A, fret 5 of the E pair
text.why: It opens on A at fret 5 of pair 1, then walks down through G, F♯ and E.

text.prompt: Which moves sound a note without the pick?
text.why: All three sound a second note with the fretting hand. The pick plays only the first.

text.prompt: Why does the fifth string sound so high?
options: It is short and tuned to high G
text.why: Being short lets it hold a high G. It sits on top of the melody like a bell.

text.prompt: Pinch, or one note at a time?
Which strings does a pinch play?
text.why: Thumb on the short fifth string and middle on string 1, at the same moment.

text.prompt: You lose the beat in the middle of a roll. What now?
options: Stop and start the bar over
Slow down until it feels right
Keep the right hand moving and rejoin
text.why: In a band the beat never waits. Keep the pattern going and catch the next bar.

text.prompt: Do you fret the fifth string for C?
text.why: The open high G belongs to the C chord, so it rings as it is. You never fret it in these lessons.

text.prompt: Where do you play F♯ in this tune?
text.why: F♯ is four frets above the open D of string 1. The fifth string is never fretted here.

text.prompt: How many times do you pick for a hammer-on?
text.why: The pick sounds the first note. The second comes from your finger striking the string.

text.prompt: Which way does your finger move in a pull-off?
options: Along the string to the next fret
text.why: Lifting straight up only stops the note. A small sideways flick plucks the open string.

text.prompt: Which move glides a fretted note up to a higher fret?
Which way does your fingernail move in clawhammer?
text.why: Clawhammer strikes down with the nail. The fingers never pluck upward.

text.prompt: Which part of bum-ditty does the thumb play?
text.why: Bum is a single note, dit is a brush and ty is the thumb on the fifth string.

text.prompt: Where do the melody notes go in bum-ditty?
text.why: The bum lands on the beat, so that is where the melody goes. Dit and ty keep the rhythm rolling.

text.prompt: Which hand shape does clawhammer use?
Half step or whole step?
Why is it called an octave?
text.why: C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C: eight letter names, counting both ends.

text.prompt: Which is wider?
text.why: A fifth spans seven half steps; a fourth spans five.

text.prompt: Which notes spell a C minor chord?
text.why: Lower the middle note of C major by a half step: E becomes E♭.

text.prompt: Why play a cadence before the note?
text.why: The chords point to do, so you can hear every other note in relation to it.

text.prompt: A melody goes do, mi, sol. How does it move?
text.why: Do to mi skips re, and mi to sol skips fa.

text.prompt: What are the next two letters after F?
text.why: F, G, then back around to A.

text.prompt: Which list goes down?
text.why: Backward through the alphabet means lower notes: E, D, C, B.

text.prompt: A4 vibrates 440 times a second. How fast does A5 vibrate?
text.why: An octave up doubles the vibration: 440 becomes 880.

text.prompt: Which two letters come right after E?
text.why: E, F, G: forward through the alphabet.

text.prompt: What does a sharp do to a note?
Which pair names the same key?
text.why: C♯ is a half step above C; D♭ is a half step below D. Same key.

text.prompt: A note on a line moves up one letter. Where does it land?
text.why: Letters alternate: line, space, line, space.

text.prompt: Where is middle C in bass clef?
options: On a ledger line above the staff
text.why: Middle C sits one ledger line above the bass staff, and one below the treble staff.

text.prompt: What's another word for a bar?
text.why: Bar and measure mean the same thing.

text.prompt: A four-beat bar has a half note and a quarter note. What fills the gap?
text.why: 2 + 1 = 3, so one beat is left: a quarter rest.

text.prompt: In C major, which steps are half steps?
options: C to D and F to G
E to F and B to C
D to E and A to B
text.why: E and F, and B and C, have no black key between them.

text.prompt: Which is the major scale recipe? (W = whole, H = half)
options: W W H W W W H
W H W W H W W
W W W H W W H
text.why: Whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half.

text.prompt: Number the scale's notes 1 to 8. Where are the half steps?
text.why: Whole, whole, then half from 3 to 4; whole, whole, whole, then half from 7 to 8.

text.prompt: Why does G major need F♯ instead of F?
options: F is too low to sing
E to F is only a half step
text.why: The recipe needs a whole step from note 6 to 7, then a half step from 7 up to G.

text.prompt: Which two sharps are in D major?
text.why: Following the recipe from D lands on F♯ as note 3 and C♯ as note 7.

text.prompt: The key signature shows B♭. Which Bs are played as B♭?
text.why: A key signature applies to every B in every octave, unless the music marks otherwise.

text.prompt: In every major scale, which step is a half step?
text.why: Whole, whole, half: the first half step falls between notes 3 and 4.

text.prompt: Which key signature belongs to G major?
Which of these fifths is smaller than perfect?
text.why: B to F spans six half steps; a perfect fifth needs seven.

text.prompt: Why is ii written in lowercase?
Which notes spell A minor?
In C major, what is ii–V–I?
text.why: ii is D minor, V is G, and I is C.

text.prompt: In F major, what is ii–V–I?
text.why: F, G, A, B♭, C: ii is G minor and V is C.

text.prompt: In ii–V–I, how do the roots move?
text.why: D down to G, then G down to C: a fifth each time.

text.prompt: In the key of E, what are the three blues chords?
text.why: In E, I is E, IV is A and V is B.

text.prompt: In D major, what is I–V–vi–IV?
text.why: In D: I is D, V is A, vi is B minor, IV is G.

text.prompt: How does a beat feel?
text.why: A beat keeps the same space between pulses, like a clock ticking.

text.prompt: You tap on 1 and 3. What happens on 2 and 4?
text.why: The beat never stops. You count through the beats you don't tap.

text.prompt: At 60 bpm, how often does the beat come?
text.why: 60 beats in 60 seconds is one beat each second.

text.prompt: The tempo goes up. What should your taps do?
options: Wait a little behind the click
text.why: Small, relaxed motions are quicker and easier to keep even.

text.prompt: What does 90 bpm mean?
text.why: bpm counts beats per minute, so 90 bpm is one and a half beats each second.

text.prompt: How do you count this pattern?
text.why: Beat 1 has two taps, 1 and. Beats 2, 3 and 4 get one tap each.

text.prompt: Your eighths sound uneven. What helps most?
options: Slow down and count out loud
Speed up until it smooths out
text.why: Slowing down gives you time to place each "and" in the middle. Counting keeps it there.

text.prompt: What do you do on a rest?
text.why: A rest takes up time just like a note. Counting it keeps your place.

text.prompt: Where is the second tap?
text.why: It sits halfway between beats 2 and 3, on the "and" of 2.

text.prompt: The first click is beat 1. Are the strong clicks on the numbers or the ands?
Which of these is syncopated?
text.why: Tapping the "and" of 2 and skipping 3 moves the weight off the beat.

text.prompt: Beat 2 is tied to beat 3. What do you do on 3?
text.why: A tie stretches one note. You count 3, but the note from beat 2 keeps sounding.

text.prompt: You tapped this pattern with a rest in Unit 3. What changes with a dot?
text.why: The taps land in the same places. Only the length of the first note changes.

text.prompt: Are the clicks in groups of two or three?
Six clicks per bar. Which meter is this?
What is an accent?
text.why: An accent is about weight, not length. The note is simply played stronger.

text.prompt: The first click is beat 1. Where are the strong clicks?
Your note wobbles and fades. What helps most?
text.why: Steady air makes a steady note. Extra volume and tension make it harder to control.

text.prompt: Timbre says you're flat. What do you do?
text.why: Flat means under the note, so lift the pitch slightly.

text.prompt: What does sharp mean?
text.why: Sharp is over the target pitch; flat is under it.

text.prompt: Your first try lands flat. What next?
text.why: Small changes find the note fastest. Lift gently and let it settle.

text.prompt: Which is a half step?
text.why: E to F has no note between them. C to D and G to A are whole steps.

text.prompt: Between which two steps is there a half step?
text.why: Mi to fa (E to F) is a half step. The other steps from do to sol are whole steps.

text.prompt: Where are the half steps in a major scale?
text.why: Mi-fa and ti-do are half steps. That pattern gives the major scale its sound.

text.prompt: A step or a skip?
Why do the two notes of an octave blend so well?
options: The top one vibrates twice as fast
text.why: The top note vibrates exactly twice as fast as the bottom one, so their waves line up.

text.prompt: What is a pickup?
options: The loudest note of a song
A note before the first full bar
text.why: A pickup leads into beat 1 of the first full bar.

text.prompt: Your long notes go flat at the end. What helps?
options: End the note sooner and breathe
text.why: Pitch sags when you run low on air. Ending a bit early keeps the whole note in tune.

text.prompt: Where does healthy vibrato come from?
options: A relaxed throat and steady breath
text.why: Vibrato appears when the voice is free and supported. Forcing it from the jaw or belly makes a wobble.

text.prompt: What's the best first goal for a new singer?
text.why: A steady tone is the foundation. Vibrato that grows from it sounds natural.

text.prompt: As you get louder, what can happen to pitch?
text.why: Extra push tends to raise the pitch, and very soft notes can sag flat. Watch the note either way.

text.prompt: What is vibrato?
text.why: Vibrato is a gentle, even wave around the note, a few times a second.

text.prompt: To sing louder, what do you add?
text.why: Breath energy makes a bigger sound without strain.

text.prompt: In a round, the second player…
text.why: Everyone plays the same melody, each starting a little later. The phrases are built to fit on top of each other.

text.prompt: What does the bass do all through the Canon?
options: Plays a new tune each time
text.why: A repeating bass like this is called a ground. Everything else in the piece is built on top of it.

text.prompt: Two notes share each beat in this tune. How do you count them?
text.why: Two even notes per beat are eighth notes. Say the number on the first and "and" on the second.

text.prompt: What does a dot after a note do?
options: Makes it half again as long
text.why: A dotted quarter lasts a beat and a half. The note after it is usually quick, to fill out the beat.

text.prompt: Silent Night is in 6/8. How are its six counts grouped?
text.why: 6/8 sways in two big beats, each split into three: one-two-three, four-five-six.

text.prompt: This tune runs from string 5 to string 1. What keeps every string in reach?
text.why: With your thumb low behind the neck, your fingers arch and reach from string 5 to string 1 without straining.

text.prompt: Does the hook climb or fall at first?
Which string is the boom for a D chord?
text.why: D's root is open string 4, the same string a D strum starts from.

text.prompt: Kite Weather plays G, D, E minor and C. Echo Canyon plays E minor, C, G and D. What changed?
text.why: Same four chords, same key. Starting on E minor puts the sad chord first, so the loop sounds darker.

text.prompt: Which of these is the four-chord loop in C?
text.why: The one, five, six and four of C are C, G, A minor and F.

text.prompt: Which of these styles swings, long-short?
text.why: Doo-wop rides a gentle swing. Punk and surf drive on straight, even eighths.

text.prompt: Bar two keeps bar one's rhythm but swaps one note. Why?
text.why: Bar two moves E up to F sharp, a note of B minor. Same rhythm, new chord, new note.

text.prompt: Which word holds over two notes in the first verse?
text.why: Fly starts on C and slides down to a long A. Singers call one syllable over several notes a melisma.

text.prompt: What happens at the end of the Toreador tune?
options: It climbs to a long E
text.why: It climbs to a long high E, the note that leads back home to A major for the march.

text.prompt: Which word dips down to the low D in the first verse?
options: Thee, in how still we see thee lie
text.why: How still we see thee lie: the tune falls to open D on thee, then lifts to B on lie.

text.prompt: Which of these tunes is the oldest?
text.why: William Croft wrote St Anne in 1708, almost 150 years before the other two.

text.prompt: How does Jupiter's tune count?
text.why: Like a slow waltz: one, two, three. Each phrase starts with two eighth notes before beat one.

text.prompt: Which two of these count in three?
options: The Last Rose of Summer and Jupiter
Hard Times and The Last Rose of Summer
text.why: The Last Rose of Summer and Jupiter are both in three. Home! Sweet Home! and Hard Times count in four.
